title: Image subtitles from discs play, drawn by the player or into the picture
description: Serves PRODUCT.md: "A 4K HDR disc rip with Dolby Vision and image subtitles, an old DVD rip ... each plays ... with the audio and subtitles they chose. No ... subtitle kind is second-class." The engine's image subtitles are carried over here, with the audit's findings on them addressed (D-20261128-audit-findings).
acceptanceCriteria: Image subtitle tracks (from Blu-ray, DVD and broadcast) are offered; a player that draws them gets them as they are, and otherwise they are drawn into the picture.
A seek anywhere, or a worker taking over, shows the subtitle that is on screen at that moment from the first frame.
A DVD-style subtitle file kept beside a film that holds several languages is still offered after its first use, and each of its languages can be picked or says why it can't.
A film with a subtitle drawn into its picture resumes cleanly after a pause of any length.
A track found unreadable is never offered and never costs a re-encode; a damaged stored track is reported as the file's and never interrupts other films on the same worker.
Proven on Media3 on Android TV and phone emulators and on hls.js in Chromium; the design states what is stored per film.
notes: Audit group 3; the several-languages file comes first within it, as the one finding that hits every affected film. That a drawn subtitle costs a re-encode is stage 3 (JS-323).
